Payer mix, non-labor expenses dragged hospital margins in September" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy">

Hospitals’ operations took another dip in September amid a slew of ongoing headwinds including weakened payer mix and rising costs, healthcare advisory firm Kaufman Hall reported alongside warnings of a “historically large portion” of the nation’s hospitals running on negative or near-zero operating margins.

The firm’s latest monthly benchmark report, released Tuesday, revealed a calendar year-to-date operating margin index of 1.4% and a single-month operating margin index of 2.4% in September, the latter of which was a decline from August’s 3.0% operating margin (all including health system allocations for shared services costs).

The performance decline wasn’t for want of patients. Daily discharges and adjusted discharges both rose 3% from August to September, and are generally above the numbers from last year. Operating room minutes per calendar day also rose 6% from August—an encouraging sign for hospitals whose surgical slowdowns had hamstrung acuity—but remain 1% below September of last year.

It has been revealed that the increased foot traffic also grew revenues, with daily net operating revenue rising 4% from August and 6% year over year while gross operating revenue rose 4% month to month and 8% year over year. Much of the increase came on the outpatient side, where daily revenue increased 5% from August and 10% compared to September 2025. Net patient service revenue per adjusted discharge was more mixed, rising 2% from August but remaining 1% below September 2025.

However, hospitals’ margins are being challenged by persistent bad debt and charity care burdens, Kaufman Hall’s data show. Daily bad debt and charity care may have remained flat from August, but is 17% higher than September 2025 and 16% higher when comparing both years’ first nine months. As a percentage of gross operating revenue, they’re 6% higher than Sept. 2025 and 8% higher year to date.

Industry observers note that on the spending side, daily total expense rose 3% from August and is 5% higher than September 2025, primarily reflecting the heightened volumes even as hospitals held their average length of stay flat month over month or 1% shorter year over year. The expenses were more pronounced on the non-labor side, where increases on a per adjusted discharge basis were higher than labor’s per adjusted discharge decline.

"Hospitals continue to operate in an environment marked by significant financial variability," Erik Swanson, managing director and Data and Analytics group leader at Kaufman Hall, mentioned in a release. “Many organizations continue to face mounting pressure from uncompensated care and rising expenses, underscoring the importance of proactive operational and financial strategies that build long-term resilience.".

Another amplifying market trend is the “bifurcation of hospital performance” often highlighted by the firm and others that monitor multi-organization financial trends, such as credit rating agencies.

"The margin gap between higher and lower-performing hospitals has widened to 19 percentage points, with a historically large portion of hospitals operating at negative or very thin margins,” the report reads. “Even slight revenue reductions threaten organizations, which face increasingly difficult decisions on future operations, care delivery, and expense control.”.

The firm encouraged hospitals to take “deliberate, proactive steps” to strengthen their financial situations, particularly as macro reimbursement trends stiffen and the site of care delivery shifts from the hospital to outpatient settings.

Kaufman Hall’s hospital reports pull data from more than 1,300 nationwide hospitals as collected by parent manufacturer Strata Decision Technology.

Accompanying the monthly hospital benchmark was also Kaufman Hall’s quarterly numbers on more than 200,000 employed physicians and advanced practice providers, which painted a much rosier picture for health system and hospital employers.

It revealed, for the first time in five years of data collection, that healthcare employers’ investment/subsidy per provider and per physician has declined year over year (by 1%), and “across every cohort, including primary care, medical specialty, surgical specialty and hospital-based specialty.”.

Kaufman Hall attributed the rare turnaround to revenue growth and sustained productivity increases that together outpaced expenses.

Recent findings suggest that "Medical groups made meaningful performance improvements this quarter, achieving gains in revenue, productivity and thoughtful workforce management," Matthew Bates, managing director and Physician Enterprise Service Line leader at Kaufman Hall, mentioned in a release. "The growing utilization of [advanced practice providers] and ongoing focus on operational and team effectiveness are helping organizations manage financial pressures while increasing access to care.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toyota's Corolla hatchback is already a pretty lovely car, but I adored driving the all-wheel drive turbocharged Corolla GR. You can imagine how great it must be with more power and less weight, as found in the GRMN. That initialism isn't just the stock ticker symbol for Garmin, it's an extremely fancy $64,000 Toyota hot hatch, and it allegedly stands for Gazoo Racing Masters of the Nürburgring. Maybe the hottest hatch of all time? I haven't yet had the pleasure of slipping behind the wheel, but my delightful (and extremely tall) colleague Logan absolutely loved their time driving it, and recommended buying one.

In a recent development, the Corolla isn't the first GRMN product in the world, as that honor belongs to the Yaris GRMN which isn't sold here. That remarked, this definitely got me thinking about what else Toyota could build if it wanted to get super serious about performance cars. Don't get me wrong, I think Toyota is building more cars for enthusiasts today than any other automaker, and there are more in the pipeline, but what's the harm in offering pumped up versions?

Given my druthers, I'd absolutely love to see an amped up Prius GRMN. The all-wheel drive Prius is already quite quick and powerful, given its economy car bent. The current generation is also quite a fetching design. I want something economical that looks good, but when I put my foot down, I want something a little quicker than the current 7-ish second 0-60 time. The AWD Prius currently uses a 150-horsepower 2-liter four-cylinder engine mated to a 111 horsepower electric motor at the front, plus a tiny 40 horsepower electric motor at the rear axle. What if Toyota wanted to get serious about acceleration and ditched the gas motor for the GRMN Corolla's 300-pony 1.6-liter three-cylinder instead? And maybe that puny rear motor could be supplanted by the 165 horse electric motor found in the base model bZ electric. Keep the same electric motor that the current Prius has in the front, you're still looking to at least double the power output from standard Prius to theoretical GRMN Prius. I like it, how about you?

Sources indicate that toyota makes a whole lot of different cars. I want to hear what your favorite hypothetical GRMN silk purse from a base model sow's ear might be. Pick a model that Toyota currently makes and give us your idea for how it could be GRMN-ified. Given that the GRMN Corolla is a two-seater with the rear seats stripped out, you can kind of go hog wild with it. Do you want to see a Sienna with aggressive track-focused aerodynamic bodywork? How about a Toyota Sequoia V8 stuffed under the hood of a GRMN-86?

Industry observers note that this is your dream workshop, and you're playing with whatever toys are already in the Toyota (or Lexus) arsenal. Because GRMN is a track-focused operation, these creations should also be intended with the dual purpose of fun driving dynamics and fast lap times. Try to keep it to a parts bin special, if you please, because there's no good game in the world without a few rules to it. Maybe you want to go hog wild with it and bring the Lexus LFA's V10 out of retirement to shove under the hood of a track-oriented Tundra sport truck? Now that would be a whole lot of street style. It's Saturday, you don't have to leave dream world just yet, so you have the entire Toyota research and development team at your beck and call, what wild track-oriented automotive monstrosity would you make them create?

Industry observers note that I don't know about you, but I'm still thinking about that time attack bZ that Toyota brought to SEMA last year. That could make a pretty cool GRMN EV.

According to recent reports, let's chat about it. Sound off in the comments below with your thoughts on engine and drivetrain swaps, and we'll discuss it. Then, I'll pick a few of my favorite responses to recap for everyone else next week.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Singer Ella Langley made history at the Country Music Awards when she set the record for the most CMA awards won by a woman in one night—so will where the hitmaker house her new trophies?

The "Choosin Texas" singer, 27, won entertainer of the year, female vocalist of the year, album of the year, single of the year, and song of the year.

When accepting her sixth award of the evening, she teased, "At this point, I'm sick of me!".

According to recent reports, “This has been the most special night. I could quit tomorrow and have the best career of my life," she added.

At one point during the evening, fellow country star Lainey Wilson joked, "I said I was gonna bring you a bedazzled broom. I knew you was gonna sweep, girl.”.

At the end of the evening, Langley posed with all of her awards as she smiled from ear to ear.

Langley will put her multiple trophies on display at her lakefront retreat, which she picked up in 2025.

In July 2025, Langley snapped up her first-ever home in her hometown of Montgomery, AL, just minutes away from her parents' home.

Langley, who lives in Nashville, TN, but was born and raised in Alabama, gushed about her newly minted purchase while speaking to Audacy, telling the radio station that she decided to make her first real estate investment in her home state because she feels most like herself when she's there.

"It just brings me back to who I am at the root of me every time I go back there. And when it comes to writing songs and being in that state of mind, I think it’s notable to have a place like that," she said.

The star noted that, while she will likely "always" live in Tennessee, which is the home of country music, she will continue to keep roots in Alabama because of how close she is to her family.

“I think I’ll always have to live in Tennessee to some extent in my life, but being from Alabama, it’s so close. It’s under four hours to get there," she added.

Though many young people might find the process of buying their first property overwhelming, Langley conceded that she was in a much more privileged position—namely because she has her own business managers who helped to oversee the entire purchase.

According to recent reports, "I honestly been having a blast. I have great business management. They just get all the phone calls, yes or no, this is what I want to do, and they figure out all the little logistics, so very thankful for them,” she added.

Langley moved to Nashville in order to pursue her musical career, relocating from her hometown in Alabama in 2019.

"The music family here is just really special; people are so willing to be a mentor or help you grow in a way I just couldn’t do back home," Langley mentioned of her latest home state during an interview with Raised Rowdy.

Previously, Langley has shared that her move to Nashville also helped her to find more freedom in her writing process, joking to Raised Rowdy that she spent much of her childhood in Alabama trying to "survive life" with two brothers.

"I grew up in the country in Alabama between two brothers, so a lot of my childhood was just trying to survive life between those two," she said.

In a recent development, "I always was trying to prove I was just as tough and fearless as they were. Being a tomboy like that, a lot of my friends ended up being guys. If you ask my band or people who know me, they’ll tell you sometimes I seem more like a guy than a girl. But I think women can still be direct, strong, and tough, without apologizing for who they are or how they think.".

Making the decision to pursue her music full time was a serious one for Langley, who dropped out of Auburn University in order to focus on her passion.

“I had a boyfriend who was in music and then his manager, they were both moving to Nashville and we’re going to live with Trey (Lewis). And I was like, well hell, I’m not staying here," she previously told CountryNow.

In a recent development, "So I called mom and dad and I said, ‘Hey, I think I want to drop out of school and move to Nashville. I’m just going to be in more debt anyways when I graduate. I mean, I’m going to go do this anyways. I would rather start it now.'".

The singer also revealed that she was warmly welcomed to Nashville.

Industry observers note that “It’s been a cool journey of finding those people for me in town that I just love and love me and believe in me and I believe in them. And so that’s what’s really kept me going a lot through this," she went on.

"And obviously my family supports me the way that they do and just love me, but that’s the thing, nobody has ever thought I was going to do anything else ….

"If you ask any of my family, they’re like, ‘Yeah, we all knew that this was what she was going to do.’ So there wasn’t ever really any question when I wanted to move.".

  • Sources indicate that kai Grünitz, Member of the Board of Management for Technical Development, Volkswagen Brand and Brand Group Core: “The GTI has been one of Volkswagen’s great success stories for 50 years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, 270 kW (367 PS), top speed of 240 km/h and 4.7 seconds from 0 to 100 km/h: With the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, Volkswagen is marking the 50th anniversary of the GTI by showing how uncompromising an electric GTI with motorsport ambitions can be. The concept car will be presented to the public next week at the Essen Motor Show (27 November to 6 December 2026). Its performance figures meet a two-door silhouette and flared wings as well as a large front splitter, diffuser and rear wing. The result: a powerful appearance and maximum downforce for fast laps. At the same time, the concept vehicle provides a preview of how the GTI idea can be further developed in the electric age.

Sources indicate that kai Grünitz, Member of the Board of Management for Technical Development, Volkswagen Brand and Brand Group Core: “The GTI has been one of Volkswagen’s great success stories for 50 years. This year, we debuted our GTI as an electric vehicle in series production for the first time. With the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, we are showing how much more potential there is in the electric GTI world. Our platform strategy and MEB+ give us the technological freedom to make even extreme concepts possible.”.

Designed for performance. The design of the upcoming ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept is based on the production model, the 166 kW (226 PS) ID. Polo GTI. In both models, the drive power is transmitted to the front axle. In the 270 kW (367 PS) ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, this power delivery is controlled – thanks in part to an electronically regulated front differential lock (VAQ) – so that the model reaches 100 km/h from a standstill in just 4.7 seconds with Launch Control. Like the drive system, the electrical infrastructure has also been adapted to the high performance of the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept. The 52 kWh high-voltage battery can provide up to 290 kW at short notice, enabling a top speed of 240 km/h. The DCC (adaptive chassis control) has also been tuned for use on the racetrack and ensures precise handling and high traction in conjunction with the front differential lock. The new ceramic brakes of the one-box brake system are also designed for high performance.

Dynamics are visible in the design. On the exterior, the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept follows the powerful clarity of the ID. Polo GTI production model, while at the same time incorporating design elements that underline the motorsport characteristics. Particularly striking features are the two-door instead of four-door silhouette, pronounced flaring of the wings by 50 millimetres in each case, a large motorsport splitter at the front, a wider rear end, a latest diffuser and a rear wing in carbon fibre that protrudes above the roof line.

Two-seater. Reduced to racing. The interior is also tailored to the racetrack, and only the basic layout of the overall cockpit has been adopted from the production model. This means there is no infotainment system, for example. The focus is solely on ergonomics and driving. The driver and front passenger sit on Recaro racing bucket seats with red 5-point harnesses. The rear and luggage compartment have been completely cleared. Instead of a rear seat system, a rollover bar painted in the GTI colour Tornado Red is integrated above and behind the front seats. The dash panel, side trims and many other details are covered in dark ArtVelours microfibre fabric with red topstitching – work that has been carried out with great precision by Volkswagen trainees. In many areas – in keeping with Volkswagen tradition – the young employees were directly involved in realisation of the concept vehicle by the Development department and designers.

According to recent reports, 550 instead of 290 newton-metres. The ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept features the high-torque APP550 motor. The special technical challenge here: this motor is actually intended for the rear of large models such as the ID. Tiguan or ID.7. It therefore had to be fitted into the smaller ID. Polo as front-wheel drive and additionally combined with an electronic front differential lock. Thomas Schmall, Member of the Board of Management Volkswagen AG for Technology, and CEO of Volkswagen Group Components: “The ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept indicates just how emotive electric mobility can be: This is made possible by our APP550, one of the most efficient electric drives in its class. Manufactured over one million times at the Group Components plant in Kassel, this drive was actually developed for larger vehicle classes. Integrating it into the Polo required millimetre precision and is a powerful example of engineering skill and teamwork at Volkswagen, from Development and Design through to our trainees who worked on the project.”.

According to recent reports, GTI from the master of modular platforms. The ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept is based on the modular electric drive (MEB+) platform with front-wheel drive. Volkswagen has used the basic technical layout of the production model and taken it to a new level of performance with a 104 kW (141 PS) more powerful electric drive. The result is the most dynamic interpretation of a front-wheel drive ID. model to date. At the other end of the scale is the Mission Efficiency, which is also based on the ID. Polo and set four world records as a particularly efficient near-production electric vehicle. Both concept vehicles show the large bandwidth offered by electric drive systems from maximum sportiness to outstanding efficiency.

It has been revealed that 2026 is the year of the GTI. Following the Golf GTI EDITION 50, the fresh ID.3 GTI (sales start early 2027) and the new ID. Polo GTI (available to order since October), the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept is making its debut this year as the fourth new model under the umbrella of the iconic GTI product brand. No other compact sports car family has been as successful worldwide for half a century now – with more than 2.5 million units sold – as the GTI models.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • When it comes to exploring enticing investment opportunities, real estate often stands out as an excellent solution for making and growing wealth.
  • In recent years, as the world has continued to evolve, the marketplace for real estate investors has evolved with it.
  • Not all real estate investments have to include purchasing actual bricks and mortar in the physical world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When it comes to exploring enticing investment opportunities, real estate often stands out as an excellent solution for making and growing wealth. No matter how the world around us changes, there will always be a demand for property in attractive areas. This has led countless people to diversify their portfolios over the years, buying rental properties, second homes, and even office spaces.

In recent years, as the world has continued to evolve, the marketplace for real estate investors has evolved with it. Today, people no longer need to buy and flip entire properties to make money. There are numerous tips for getting started and ways you can start your journey into the property world, and some options are actually simpler and more affordable than you might expect. Here are some of the best, most interesting ways to invest in real estate, if you want to avoid the traditional buy and flip strategy.

Not all real estate investments have to include purchasing actual bricks and mortar in the physical world. The digital landscape has evolved drastically in recent years, introducing latest opportunities for innovative entrepreneurs to make money buying virtual assets. As the concept of the metaverse continues to gain traction, digital real estate is growing increasingly attractive.

With digital real estate, companies purchase a section of the blockchain in a metaverse landscape, where they can build online experiences, or simply store other assets. In 2021, sales on four of the biggest metaverse platforms for real estate reached a whopping $501 million. This indicates learning how to invest in digital real estate could be a worthwhile strategy for any consumer. Not only is it potentially profitable, but the digital real estate also requires less work to manage and maintain than a physical house or property.

In a recent development, even if you’re not familiar with this form of property-based investing, you probably know the term crowdfunding. Made popular by sites like GoFundMe and Kickstarter, the crowdfunding strategy involves individuals pooling their resources together to fund a product or business. In the real estate world, investors can work together to purchase a property, such as a corporate space, warehouse, or block of flats, reducing the initial cost of a purchase.

The approach allows investors to participate in products that would have been impossible to access in the past because of high capital requirements. Individuals can use this strategy to diversify their portfolios with a variety of different locations and property types. Plus, you’ll earn a passive income through rental profits, and property appreciation.

According to recent reports, another real estate investment strategy gaining increasing attention in recent years is REITs. These are basically investment vehicles responsible for owning and operating income-generating assets, such as rental properties and office blocks. They’re traded on traditional stock exchanges and provide individuals with an opportunity to invest in the market, without directly owning a property or having to manage the investment themselves.

It has been revealed that REITs can come with several attractive features, including regular distributions of dividends, and the ability to explore a range of different sectors. You can even use this strategy to spread your portfolio across industrial, residential, and commercial properties. They’re also a highly liquid investment option, making them appealing to beginners.

Finally, one interesting way to invest in real estate, without buying a physical property outright, is to spend some of your money on shares in PropTech startups. PropTech, or Property Technology startups, are companies focused on developing tools and real estate designed to transform the property landscape. They develop things like property management solutions, smart home technology, and virtual reality applications for tours.

According to recent reports, if you already have experience in the world of stocks and shares, investing in a PropTech company could be an excellent way to utilize your existing knowledge and diversify your portfolio. It’s also a chance to get your foot in the door with a company that’s actively disrupting the real estate space, and the market as we know it.

Investing in property has become a much more diverse and versatile opportunity for individuals in recent years. No matter how much money you can afford to spend, or where your expertise lies, you can find plenty of ways to expand your portfolio with disruptive real-estate investment strategies.

The Fierce Healthcare team is on the ground at HLTH 2026. Stick with this news tracker to catch all the highlights from the show floor, and click here for additional coverage from the conference.

DJ and music producer Steve Aoki told the HLTH audience that his father's passing was the catalyst for his interest in healthcare.

Learning more about what caused his death, and if it could have been prevented, drew him to the impacts of dementia and cancer. And in exploring that, he mentioned he decided he wanted to invest in the people who are pursuing the "science fiction concepts" in healthcare, and support cutting edge innovation.

Aoki remarked that his celebrity status made it easier to get into a room with people leading the charge on innovation, and learn as much as he could.

"I was just as intrigued as working with a big artist in the studio or playing a big show," he noted.

It was with that learning that he established Aoki Foundation, an organization he remarked is dedicated to bringing back the science and investing in what's next.

"People are excited about science fiction, about the possibility of doing things that are impossible," Aoki said. "And I feel like the superheroes of our time are like right right in our midst, and it's about it's about highlighting their journey and giving them a spotlight.".

It’s been several weeks since Doximity integrated Wolters Kluwer Health’s UpToDate into its AI clinical decision support tool.

Doximity VP of Clinical AI Partnerships Kamal Menghrajani, M.D., told Fierce Healthcare at HLTH said the integration gives her “a little bit more confidence” in her own practice.

“Now I can use UpToDate to supplement and feel like what I'm doing at the point of care really is the best thing for the patient,” she said.

Menghrajani, who previously served as assistant director for cancer innovation and public health at the White House, took on the role with Doximity approximately four months ago.

“[I get to] be the physician voice and represent the interests of doctors within the firm,” she stated. “And think about what it looks like to actually take the tools we're building and serve doctors better.”.

In a recent development, menghrajani said the rapid expansion of the company’s AI suite has been a key takeaway, adding that a focus for the company is what physicians want out of AI. “I've seen Doximity evolve to meet all of those needs,” Menghrajani said.

It has been revealed that as a range of AI tools saturate the industry, Menghrajani noted the biggest use she has seen amongst clinicians is ambient scribes. “I think that has been a real game changer in terms of actual practice,” she said.

On the HLTH show floor, you may have noticed a theme.

Las Vegas is abuzz with the upcoming Formula 1 race, which is taking place on Saturday, Nov. 21. The city has been preparing for the Las Vegas Grand Prix, which is on the Strip, for weeks, and HLTH is taking place at one of the hubs for F1 excitement, The Venetian.

It has been revealed that so at this year's conference, each of the stages is themed around racing: the Velocity Stage, the Ferrari Stage, the Monacco Stage. And each breakout track is referred to as a "circuit." In the conference livery, HLTH mascot Petunia is show driving a race car.

Industry observers note that activations on the show floor also play into the F1 theme. A racing simulation game is set up for attendees near the Pharma Force stage, and swag giveaways allude to the race.

Panelists at a HLTH session discussing the uptake of ICHRA — scratch that, CHOICE — faced a challenge around the nomenclature.

Individual coverage health reimbursement arrangements, or ICHRAs, represent a growing area of interest for employers and insurers participating in the individual market. But on Sept. 3, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services confirmed that it would instead refer to these models as CHOICE, which stands for Custom Health Option and Individual Care Expense.

Recent findings suggest that in these models, an employer offers enrollees a stipend to purchase coverage on the individual market rather than securing a traditional employer-sponsored initiative. ICHRA (or CHOICE) has gained traction with employers that may otherwise struggle to offer health coverage.

According to recent reports, moderator Joseph Mercer, senior managing director at Marwood Group, joked that the panelists had all agreed to call these prepares CHOICE rather than ICHRA. But throughout the session, slip-ups drew a chuckle.

Even the panel's title made reference to the evolution of the name: "The ICHRA (CHOICE) Debate.".

Healthcare platform Simple HealthKit revealed Tuesday a partnership with Waters Corporation to expand access to at-home cervical cancer screening.

The collaboration aims to expand access to BD’s Onclarity HPV Self-Collection Kit, which is tested with the BD Onclarity HPV Assay  and Simple HealthKit's artificial intelligence-powered direct-to-patient-provider platform.

Sources indicate that "We envision a future where personalized, world-class healthcare is accessible to everyone, regardless of where they live,” remarked Sheena Menezes, Ph.D, Simple HealthKit CEO and co-founder, in a statement. “Our AI-powered direct-to-patient and provider platform brings that vision to life by connecting people with the right education, intelligent personalized engagement, and clinical care at every step.”.

Menezes continued, “Through partnerships with innovators like Waters Corporation, we are empowering individuals to take charge of their health while making seamless, personalized care accessible at scale.”.

Oura CEO joined Counsel Health CEO and founder Muthu Alagappan Tuesday morning to discuss the wearable organization’s recently announced $625 million acquisition of the virtual primary care company.

Hale remarked Oura selected Counsel as a partner after reviewing the landscape, and “uptake” from customers was “very positive.”.

Sources indicate that “We started talking seriously about taking that partnership,” Hale said. “And while we had been dating for a while, we thought maybe it was time to get married.”.

Hale mentioned the agreement was “really driven” by Oura customers using Counsel in “really novel and interesting ways.”.

Alagappan remarked one of the most exciting aspects of the partnership is the potential impact of AI-fueled access to physicians on preventive care, adding the daily engagement of wearing Oura rings struck him.

“The buy-in from almost all people is tremendous, and so you enable primary care with the thing that has always been missing, which is engagement,” he mentioned. “And now we have a way to incentivize, motivate patients to make the changes that actually prevent disease, alongside the screenings and lab tests that are also very important.”.

During a Monday fireside chat, CMS Deputy Administrator and Chief Product Officer Amy Gleason noted HHS and OCR colleagues “have done an amazing job” at looking at the concern to “remove friction from the patient experience.”.

Sources indicate that gleason said there are three main components of the rule: the designation of a “personal health app,” identity verification and speed. “It should be almost instantaneous with electronic data, and it also indicates that this information is free to the patient,” she said.

Throughout the session with Zus Health CEO and co-founder Jonathan Bush, Gleason also touted the agency’s voluntary CMS Health Tech Ecosystem initiative.

“The idea of this was to stop waiting on regulation, like healthcare does for some reason, and to just charge forward and get the technology and people that are willing to go faster to work on it,” Gleason stated. “And we set up a bunch of different technology working groups that are really about taking the friction out of the system.”.

Evvy CEO and co-founder Priyanka Jain spoke with Fierce Healthcare Monday about research gaps in women’s health and how her company looks to bridge them through vaginal microbiome testing.

Jain said women were excluded from medical research from 1977 to 1993 after a drug being prescribed off-label for morning sickness was causing birth defects, adding the ramifications ar still being seen today.

Industry observers note that “Women to this day are diagnosed on average four years later than men across over 700 diseases,” Jain stated. “And it's hard to not point right back to the fact that we didn't study women until 1993.”.

In a recent development, to bridge these gaps, Evvy offers an at-home vaginal health test with clinician-reviewed results and personalized treatment plans. “If we've essentially never studied women, then there must be so many biomarkers in the female body that we under leverage in our definition of health and disease, and so that's our focus,” Jain remarked.

Jain added Evvy uses AI and precision medicine to “actually predict the right treatment programs” for each patient using the biomarkers.

And, Jain said women’s health needs attention, awareness and funding when asked about recent Trump administration initiatives to focus on women’s health.

In a recent development, “I’m really excited to see the attention and awareness that has been happening,” Jain stated. “But now we need to actually move dollars.”.

Department of Health and Human Services Chief Counselor Chris Klomp stated the administration is focused on bringing in top tech talent as it looks to make the massive, but aging, government insurance system work better.

According to recent reports, klomp spoke on a panel Monday morning at HLTH, where he discussed the challenges in harvesting the data necessary to transform Medicare, Medicaid and other key government programs. Klomp was recently nominated to serve as Deputy Secretary at HHS and is a rising star in the White House.

In a recent development, he said that technology can play a critical role in accelerate processes that have been historically inefficient and time consuming. At the Food and Drug Administration, for example, tech is hastening the process of developing drugs and making approvals, a timeline that previously taken a decade or more.

But embracing technology in this way isn't compromising safety for these medications, Klomp stated.

In addition, he said the administration is leaning on the personal nature of healthcare to bring in workers with the tech know-how necessary to drive critical advancements and change.

According to recent reports, "Most people don't care about healthcare unless you work in it," he said. "People also start to care about healthcare when you lose your health, or someone you love loses their health. And than it rapidly becomes the most important thing to you.".

"We're using that as an opportunity to drive requirement, drive amazing talent," Klomp remarked.

Houston Methodist announced Monday it has expanded its advanced inpatient monitoring care to include rural hospitals throughout Kansas.

Participating hospitals will provide patients with Medtronic’s BioButton, which continuously monitors vital signs, while the Houston Methodist remote monitoring team will review the data and work with bedside nurses.

Recent findings suggest that the vital monitoring devices are used at all eight acute-care hospitals in the Houston Methodist system, across more than 2,500 inpatient beds, according to the Nov. 11 announcement.

Industry observers note that “Innovation is most meaningful when we identify patient needs, take what works or doesn't work and find fresh ways to extend the positive impact,” said Sara Loewy, Houston Methodist virtual care vice president, in a statement. “What we’ve built in Houston has the potential to reach much further. By thoughtfully extending this model into new care settings, our goal with this program is to demonstrate how our system’s existing technology and clinical expertise can strengthen access and improve outcomes in rural communities.”.

Loewy added the expansion is an opportunity to “explore how the capabilities of a major health system can be shared across geographic boundaries.”.

While 72% of health tech startups lead with “AI-powered” in their descriptors, zero surveyed venture capitalists in a fresh report from HLTH and SolComms noted the phrase increased their confidence.

Independently surveyed health tech reporters also ranked “AI-powered” as one of the most overused phrases in pitching–in addition to “revolutionizing/transforming” and “disrupting.”.

Alongside these survey responses, researchers compared–and scored–the messaging of 72 U.S.-based, venture-backed health tech startups at series A to series C for the “Healthtech Attention Economy Report.” Startups’ messaging across their website and social media was scored on four main dimensions: clarity, differentiation, proof and policy awareness.

SolComms Vice President of HealthTech Isabella Morreale said in a statement the companies that will get attention within the next year “are leading with proof, not adjectives.”.

“That means speaking to clinical data, measurable outcomes, and validation from third parties,” Morreale mentioned. “Founder-led storytelling will also continue to stand out. Among the data, one common through-thread for investor and reporter interest was founders with a real point of view on the industry.”.

Morreale continued, “Reporters don't need another tech giant description; they need a source who can help them explain what's happening in healthcare.”.

Less than half (42.2%) of patients say communications from healthcare providers “often” or “always” feel relevant to their needs, a fresh report from Lirio found.

Industry observers note that analysts at the behavioral science and AI-powered behavioral intelligence platform polled 1,500 adults across the U.S. for the survey. While 58% of respondents report communications not consistently feeling relevant to their needs, 55.6% rate overall communication experiences with healthcare organizations as “good” or “excellent.”.

When asked why healthcare communications are ignored altogether, respondents report generic or irrelevant content (24.4%), too many similar messages (21.8%) and confusing, jargon-filled messages (18.8%) as top reasons.

Nearly half of respondents (47.9%) report the potential value of more personalized, better-timed messages as an “8, 9 or 10” for how much it could help them make better care decisions and stay engaged.

Lirio Chief Behavioral Officer Amy Bucher, Ph.D., said in a statement patients “are not rejecting healthcare communications outright.”.

Sources indicate that “They are telling us, in specific and measurable terms, that the system is talking at them instead of to them,” Bucher said. "The instinct in healthcare has long been to solve engagement with more outreach - more emails, more reminders, more portals. This data shows that volume is not the problem. What is missing is relevance — content and timing designed for where a specific patient is in their own health journey, rather than a single message broadcast to an entire population.”.

Bucher added the healthcare organizations that close the communication gap will be “the ones that use behavioral data to determine the right message, the right channel, and the right moment for each individual patient, which is the model Lirio was built to deliver.".

Community-based specialty palliative care provider Vynca is expanding its reach into four more states.

Recent findings suggest that patients will now be able to access Vynca’s services in Georgia, Hawaii, Latest Jersey and Texas. Vynca is one of the first practices approved to provide services under New Jersey’s Community-Based Palliative Care Medicaid benefit, released in April, according to the Nov. 16 announcement.

Founded in 2013, the organization’s hybrid care model combines in-home visits with virtual clinical support and predictive technology, and executives say it has shown 43% fewer emergency department visits and 52% less hospital stays within six months of enrollment.

It has been revealed that “Health plan and government program leaders understand the value of community-based palliative care for people with serious illness,” said Darren Schulte, M.D., Vynca CEO, in a statement. “Our expansion in four key states reflects growing momentum to expand specialty outpatient palliative care outside of hospices. The key is to broaden access and convenience for the entire eligible population by offering home-based options. Too often, patients are limited to seeking palliative care when available in the community, at hospital-based clinics and facilities.”.

Why Cars Need To Be Driven To Stay In Peak Condition

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
  • Sources indicate that humans anthropomorphize cars in many different and often goofy ways, but there is one thing we have in common: sedentary lifestyles are bad for both of us.
  • Of course, life happens and sometimes that extra project car that you're "definitely going to have running next week" sits for weeks, months, or even years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

Sources indicate that humans anthropomorphize cars in many different and often goofy ways, but there is one thing we have in common: sedentary lifestyles are bad for both of us. Much like neglecting to stretch those hammies can add strain to certain movements, leaving your car untouched can cause components to seize up, and both can be a major pain in the butt. While time comes for us all and everything will eventually deteriorate from age, keeping active can still help keep us in peak shape and prevent additional concerns from arising.

Of course, life happens and sometimes that extra project car that you're "definitely going to have running next week" sits for weeks, months, or even years. However, this can have real consequences. Leaving your car stationary too long can result in brake corrosion, battery problems, fuel system issues, and leaks. All can lead to reduced performance or potentially costly repairs.

According to recent reports, thankfully, many of these problems can be mitigated by simply using your vehicle for what it is designed for — regular driving! Taking a weekly cruise that lasts about 20 to 30 minutes, per AAA guidance, will help keep your vehicle's fluids flowing, parts lubricated, and battery charged. Turns out, hitting those favorite back roads is actually good for both you and your car.

So what does regular driving help prevent? Well, in as little as a day or two, a thin layer of rust can form on the brake rotors of a parked car. Fortunately, this is mostly cosmetic and normal driving clears this up after a few stops, but over extended periods of time corrosion can set in and seize up braking components.

Fuel that sits in your gas tank lasts about three to six months before it starts to break down. In older cars with metal fuel tanks, condensation can collect and start to rust the tank out from the inside. Aged fuel and moisture in your fuel system can lower octane, gum up fuel injectors, and lead to reduced performance. Keeping your fuel tank full (in this economy?) and cycled through every few months will help mitigate fuel system complications.

An issue that may require immediate intervention is a weak crank or no start from a dead battery. Batteries naturally lose charge with time, and even more so depending on battery age or if there are any parasites drawing current when the vehicle is off. Additionally, cold weather reduces a battery's cranking power on top of the natural battery discharge. Routine driving helps keep your battery topped off via the alternator so your car is ready.

Sources indicate that tires and belts will eventually need replacing. You may even find a flat spot in a tire that's sitting for too long. Seals and gaskets that keep fluids in place can dry up and crack when not driven enough to keep everything conditioned, soft, and flexible, which can cause leaks throughout your vehicle's powertrain. Depending on the seal and severity of the leak, this may require repair and keep your vehicle stationary even longer.

Industry observers note that if you know your car is going to be sitting for a while, there are a few steps you can take to protect your car. I grew up in the Northeast, where it's common to put away the "nice" car for a few months over the winter so it doesn't get destroyed by road salt. Indoor storage is optimal for protection from the elements, but I'm no Rockefeller and my cars get parked outside.

The annual ritual involves topping off the tank and adding a fuel stabilizer to prevent fuel degradation. Attaching a trickle charger keeps a low current fed to the battery and helps it stay ready to go. Changing the oil prior to storage will remove contaminants from the engine as an added layer of protection. A good cleaning inside and out can keep blemishes or stains from setting in. With that prep out of the way, you should be safe to get through the season.

When the time comes to start your car after it has been sitting for a while, do a quick visual inspection. Check for underinflated or flat tires, the presence of animals, and any latest leaks. If the tires are okay, fluids are at normal levels, there aren't any pools below your car or new inhabitants, and your battery isn't dead, you should be good to go. Drive it easy until the engine comes up to temp and listen for any new or unusual sounds. Just like humans, keeping your car in peak shape requires attention. Doing so will keep both you and your car happier and healthier for many more miles.

energyRe Will Continue as Construction Manager Through Commercial Operation; Sale Reflects Strength of the Firm’s South Carolina Development Platform; Transaction Expected to Close in First Quarter of 2027.

energyRe today announced that it has agreed to sell 100% of a portfolio of utility-scale solar projects in South Carolina to Enel Green Power North America, Inc. (EGPNA). The projects have a combined total capacity of roughly 317 MWdc of fresh generating capacity across the Palmetto State. The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to customary conditions, including required U.S. regulatory approvals.

Sources indicate that “This transaction is a strong validation of the projects we have built in South Carolina and of the team that developed them,” said Ryan Brown, Chief Operating Officer at energyRe. “Enel Green Power is a world-class owner and operator, and we are pleased to hand these projects to a partner that shares our commitment to delivering reliable, affordable power to South Carolina homes and businesses. Our team will remain on the ground as construction manager to see these projects through to commercial operation.”.

As part of the transaction, energyRe will continue to serve as construction manager through commercial operation.

energyRe has broken ground on approximately 450 MW in the last year and has nearly 700 MW in operation or late-stage development. The tech giant’s 1.8+ GW portfolio spans 20 projects in South Carolina, North Carolina, Nebraska, and Oklahoma.

Teladoc Health is expanding its Comprehensive Weight Care program with a new option that allows employers to contribute to GLP-1 costs outside of traditional pharmacy benefit designs.

Through the upcoming offering, employers can give access to medications from Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk—accompanied by support from licensed professionals, personalized lifestyle coaching, artificial intelligence-enabled food logging and more.

With each initiative year, employers will set a fixed payment per employee per fill that applies consistently across covered medications, the firm noted. Employees then pay the remaining balance for each fill. Teladoc manages eligibility, program oversight and consolidated invoicing.

Pharmacy claims are administered on a 100% pass-through basis, including eligibility verification and audit-ready claims documentation.

Moreover, employers can opt in to tie contributions to program engagement, using metrics like food logging and regular weigh-ins, executives say.

The offering is available now, with initial contracted clients slated to launch programs for their employees beginning Jan. 1, 2027.

“Employers want to provide benefits that help their workforce achieve their health goals and need flexible strategies that work for their organizations,” remarked Kelly Bliss, Teladoc Health U.S. Group Health president, in a statement. “We are helping employers meet the needs of their employees while providing greater predictability and transparency around healthcare spending. Importantly, we give people a trusted path to high-quality care and affordable access to FDA-approved, authentic medication for meaningful, sustained health outcomes.”.

Alongside the announcement, the tech giant also unveiled upcoming research examining two years of weight-loss outcomes among nearly 23,000 members enrolled in its programs.

Results indicated “clinically meaningful weight loss” increased over time, with 47.7% of members achieving at least 5% weight loss by 24 months. And among those who lost weight during their first year, 53% continued losing additional weight during the second.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

JJA ESS has launched its own battery passport data platform to support lifecycle information management and help companies prepare for upcoming EU regulations. The platform is hosted in the tech giant’s own cloud environment, giving the team direct responsibility for data policies, access permissions, and future updates.

Industry observers note that according to the EU Battery Regulation, from February 18, 2027, battery passports are mandatory for batteries used in light vehicles (LMTs), electric vehicles, and industrial batteries with a capacity exceeding 2 kWh that are placed on the market or put into service. Further requirements will follow.

A battery passport is a digital data record linked to a single physical battery. A QR code and a unique identifier based on the ISO/IEC 15459 series connect the data record to the battery, enabling access to information throughout its entire lifecycle. This can include product identity, material composition, CO₂ footprint, recycled content, performance and durability, condition, supply chain due diligence, and end-of-life disposal. Taken together, these data points support consistent information management from product identification to the end of the product lifecycle.

Industry observers note that for manufacturers, the challenge lies not simply in creating a QR code. The data must be traceable back to its source, up-to-date, and accessible in accordance with regulatory and business requirements. Companies must also manage access to sensitive information and comply with regulations governing cross-border data transfers and trade secrets. This balance is particularly relevant for companies operating in multiple markets. When companies utilize a third-party platform, its functionality, access to data fields, and interoperability can be determined by the provider’s configuration and service model.

Recent findings suggest that JA ESS developed the platform internally and hosts it in its own cloud environment. Data policies, access permissions, and future platform updates are managed by the JA ESS internal team. This team ensures compliance with EU regulations regarding data access, presentation, and updates, while also giving JA ESS greater control over data management. The platform can also evolve as regulatory requirements change and real-world applications provide further insights.

JA ESS is the energy storage business unit under the JA brand. As a central component of JA’s energy storage strategy, JA ESS offers a wide range of FTM and BTM applications with safe, efficient, intelligent, and customized solutions for the large-scale, commercial, and industrial sectors as well as the residential market.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Thanksgiving is the perfect time for loved ones to gather over a delicious, hearty meal.
  • Recent findings suggest that according to the American Farm Bureau, the average cost of a 10-person holiday dinner will rise by 6% from 2025 to $5.86 per person.
  • And unfortunately, the higher price tag doesn’t stop at the grocery store.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thanksgiving is the perfect time for loved ones to gather over a delicious, hearty meal. But in 2026, that feast could come with a higher price tag than we’d like.

Recent findings suggest that according to the American Farm Bureau, the average cost of a 10-person holiday dinner will rise by 6% from 2025 to $5.86 per person. That’s because staples like turkey, milk, rolls, and cranberries have shot up in price.

And unfortunately, the higher price tag doesn’t stop at the grocery store. You may also notice a spike in your utility bills as your home’s systems are forced to work harder to keep everyone comfortable.

The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) found that the average family already uses over 300 gallons of water per day at home. With increased usage from additional showers, dishwashing, and hand-washing that are typical during the holidays, costs are sure to climb.

“Having guests over greatly drives up money spent on groceries, but it also drives up utility costs. Preparing all of that food often involves keeping ovens and burners running for multiple hours and using large amounts of water in both the cooking and cleaning processes,” explains Carrie Barnard, founder and recipe developer at Eating on a Dime.

Fortunately, it’s still possible to enjoy Thanksgiving without breaking the bank. A bit of planning and creativity can help keep your grocery expenses and utility bill in check.

Where you live can also impact how much you spend this Thanksgiving.

The American Farm Bureau found that the 10-person classic dinner in the Northeast is about 5% higher than the national average of $61.57.

Sources indicate that costs in the West ($58.74) and Midwest ($56.89) are closer to the national average. And if you live in the South, you could expect to pay around $54.33.

There are a few reasons for these cost differences.

“They largely have to do with supply chains, since different regions require different imports, and these imprints cost more the further they travel,” says Barnard.

Since the Northeast is generally colder, it relies more heavily on imports for many Thanksgiving staples, which leads to a higher cost for consumers. Also, the Northeast typically has higher operating costs for businesses, meaning that grocery prices are often higher.

“However, prices vary widely between different stores, and many of them offer special holiday promotions, so there are usually savings to be found,” Barnard adds.

While grocery and energy costs may be higher this Thanksgiving, these tips can help reduce them and enjoy the holiday without overspending.

Jim Wang, founder at Wallet Hacks in Fulton, MD, suggests exploring promotions at your local supermarkets and groceries.

“Many stores know consumers are being squeezed and often try to put out promos around Thanksgiving. They may offer the turkey at a low cost to get you to make your entire holiday purchase there,” Wang explains.

Depending on how you celebrate Thanksgiving and who attends your meal, a potluck might make sense.

“Every year, we do a potluck with friends and everyone brings something to share. This defrays the costs across everyone and while you don't end up with nearly as many leftovers, that's also excess spending you can avoid, especially if Thanksgiving leftovers don't excite you,” indicates Wang.

If you’re hosting, be a bit more conservative about how much everyone will eat.

“Sometimes we get concerned about having guests leave hungry and we make too much as a result,” Wang says.

Industry observers note that it’s perfectly OK to make less of the more expensive items, like proteins, and bigger portions of sides that they can fill up on. Chances are your guests may prefer those sides to the turkey anyway.

Barnard tries to use her air fryer and slow cooker rather than my full oven when possible.

“These appliances are highly versatile and able to cook a wide variety of dishes, and they consume much less energy in the process,” explains Barnard.

Unlike ovens, which leak out heat and consume more energy the more you open the door to check on your food, air fryers and slow cookers cook things promptly and efficiently with low energy.

“I try to only use the oven when it’s required due to the size or amount of food involved,” Barnard adds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While many Americans are struggling to meet their basic needs, automakers are moving further upmarket. Porsche's mid-engined Mission S supercar concept, for example, is aimed at an ultra-wealthy clientele, with an estimated $500,000 starting price for the production model. And Jay Leno has something to say about this.

Industry observers note that during an interview with TBPN on YouTube, Leno noted Porsche was "moving upscale" with the Mission S: "They want to be like Ferrari. Sell fewer cars [for] more money to fewer people." In the old days, he noted, "A Ferrari had 800 miles and Porsche had 60,000. A Corvette, same thing." And back then, when people used to hold shootouts to find out which car was the fastest, "the only ones that demonstrated up would be Corvette and Porsche. Everybody else just didn't." Nowadays, Leno continued, people "buy a GT3 and [say,] 'I'm putting it away.'" He added, "Porsches have always been expensive, but they're not rare. There's a lot of them around.".

And while Leno mentions how someone reasonably financially successful could still aspire to own a Corvette, the lineup has gone fairly upmarket, especially with the ZR1X in the mix — although the ZR1X's starting price of roughly $230,000 is considerably lower than those of most modern Ferraris and Lamborghinis, it's still a pretty expensive automobile.

Leno concluded that this strategy of selling fewer but pricier cars is spreading across the auto industry and, more broadly, the economy as a whole. "You're either Motel 6 or the Four Seasons. ... We have no middle class anymore. And that's the sad thing.".

Recent findings suggest that there's no official definition of the middle class, at least not one that's widely agreed upon. The Pew Research Center defines middle-income households as those with an income (adjusted for household size) that's between two-thirds and double that of the U.S. median household income. Upper-income households earn more than double the median, while lower-income households earn less than two-thirds of it. By that measure, 61% of Americans were part of the middle class in 1971, with that share dropping to 51% by 2023.

It has been revealed that in fact, the share of household income held by the middle class has fallen in almost every decade since 1970. Middle-income households held 62% of all U.S. household income in 1970, but just 43% in 2022. Upper-income households, meanwhile, saw a massive gain in their share, jumping from 29% to 48%.

The middle-class decline can also be attributed to the pace at which income grew. Inflation-adjusted incomes across all tiers improved between 1970 and 2022, but not at the same rate. Upper-income households saw 78% growth, compared with just 60% for middle-income households. Lower-income folks saw the least growth (55%). In 2024, the median income of an upper-income household was $278,800, versus $115,900 for middle-income and $38,400 for lower-income households, according to Pew's 2026 report. And while upper-income households had 6.8 times the typical income of lower-income households in 2001, that number had risen to 7.3 by 2024.

Recent findings suggest that it's deeply concerning how new car sales are booming for the rich and falling for everyone else. Some of our readers have shared how their finances are holding them back from buying a new car in 2026, and they are certainly not alone.

Perhaps Jay's take on the middle class being nonexistent is a bit of a stretch. But as you can tell, income inequality is real. According to the Economic Policy Institute, between 1979 and 2023, the average annual earnings of the bottom 90% of workers saw cumulative growth of 44%, while the top 0.1% posted staggering growth of 354%. Although Americans earning an hourly wage were getting bigger paychecks than in the '70s, their purchasing power had remained largely unchanged after you factor in inflation, per a 2018 study from Pew. And according to data gathered by Statista, average real wages were down 0.8% in July 2026 compared with January 2021.

Sources indicate that no wonder there's an affordability crisis. The data indicates that President Trump's repeated claims of it being "fake" and a "hoax" couldn't be further from the truth, and plenty of working families can attest to that.

The tool can triage concerns on a range of topics, from questions about medication and benefits to pharmacy experience challenges.

In a recent development, if the AI guide can't address the individual's needs, they can choose to be connected to live support to find a solution. Optum noted about 80% of conversations using the tool led to a resolution without needing a live advocate.

The final new launch aims to support cash-pay options, according to the announcement.

Industry observers note that optum Price Wise will offer members a complete cost breakdown, including the price of a drug and any fees. That total, all-in price allows members to fully understand what their options may be and make the choice that works best for them at the pharmacy counter.

#42132. Alzheimer’s may have early warning signs outside the brain

Alzheimer’s may have early warning signs outside the brain

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1445 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Alzheimer's disease is best known for its effects on memory and thinking, but new research suggests that some symptoms may develop in a surprising place: outside the brain.
  • Scientists at the University of Central Florida (UCF) have discovered that genetic mutations associated with Alzheimer's can interfere with the nerves that control muscle movement, even without involvement from the brain or spinal cord.
  • The discovery raises the possibility that movement difficulties could provide earlier warning signs of the disease and that treatments focused exclusively on the brain may overlook key problems elsewhere in the body.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alzheimer's disease is best known for its effects on memory and thinking, but new research suggests that some symptoms may develop in a surprising place: outside the brain.

Scientists at the University of Central Florida (UCF) have discovered that genetic mutations associated with Alzheimer's can interfere with the nerves that control muscle movement, even without involvement from the brain or spinal cord. The findings could help explain why some people with Alzheimer's experience changes in walking, balance, or coordination long before noticeable memory problems emerge.

The discovery raises the possibility that movement difficulties could provide earlier warning signs of the disease and that treatments focused exclusively on the brain may overlook key problems elsewhere in the body.

The research was led by James Hickman, a professor at UCF's Nanoscience Technology Center, and Research Professor Xiufang "Nadine" Guo, working alongside scientists at the healthcare technology company Hesperos. Funded by the National Institutes of Health's National Institute on Aging, the study used laboratory systems built from human cells to investigate how inherited Alzheimer's mutations affect movement. The findings were published in Alzheimer's & Dementia: The Journal of the Alzheimer's Association.

"Motor deficits may be an earlier indication [of Alzheimer's]," Guo says. "If we can detect those changes and intervene earlier, that could help delay the onset of central nervous system symptoms.".

Why Alzheimer's Symptoms May Appear Before Memory Loss.

Alzheimer's is generally associated with progressive memory loss, confusion, and declining cognitive abilities. However, doctors have also observed that some patients develop physical symptoms, including changes in balance, coordination, and gait (manner of walking), years before clear cognitive difficulties become apparent.

These observations have raised an important question: Are such movement problems simply a consequence of damage occurring in the brain, or could Alzheimer's also interfere directly with nerves elsewhere in the body?

To investigate, the UCF team focused on familial Alzheimer's, a rare inherited form of the disease that typically develops earlier in life (from 40 to 65 years of age) than the more common form.

Their experiments revealed that motor neurons carrying mutations linked to familial Alzheimer's could disrupt the connections responsible for controlling muscles, even when the brain and spinal cord were completely absent from the experimental system.

Industry observers note that motor neurons are specialized nerve cells that transmit signals to muscles, telling them when to contract and produce movement. The upcoming findings suggest that Alzheimer's mutations can interfere with this process directly, rather than affecting movement only through damage to the brain.

It has been revealed that "This is the first time it's been demonstrated that deficits in the peripheral nervous system can arise directly from these mutations," Hickman says. "It means drugs that target the brain may not fix problems in the rest of the body.".

The peripheral nervous system includes the nerves located outside the brain and spinal cord. These nerves carry signals between the central nervous system and the rest of the body, helping control movement, sensation, and other essential functions.

Guo also points out that preserving the ability to move could have benefits beyond physical health. Regular physical activity is associated with better cognitive well-being, so protecting motor function may also help support brain health.

How a Miniature Human Cell System Revealed the Discovery.

To examine the relationship between Alzheimer's mutations and muscle movement, the scientists used an innovative laboratory platform known as "human-on-a-chip" technology.

It has been revealed that developed and manufactured through Hesperos, a manufacturer co-founded by Hickman, these miniature systems bring different types of human cells together under controlled conditions. They allow researchers to recreate specific biological functions and observe how diseases interfere with them.

Unlike conventional laboratory experiments that examine isolated cells, these systems can reproduce notable interactions between different tissues. They also provide an alternative to animal models, which do not always accurately reflect how human diseases behave.

For this study, the team created a miniature model of the neuromuscular junction, the connection where a motor neuron communicates with a muscle cell.

The model was deliberately designed without a brain or spinal cord. This was a crucial part of the experiment because it allowed the researchers to investigate whether Alzheimer's-related changes could cause movement problems independently of the central nervous system.

According to recent reports, the scientists combined healthy muscle cells with motor neurons derived from stem cells that carried genetic mutations associated with familial Alzheimer's disease. Stem cells are cells that can develop into specialized types of cells, making them valuable tools for studying human diseases in the laboratory.

The researchers then examined how effectively the altered nerve cells communicated with otherwise healthy muscle tissue.

In a recent development, the results highlighted that the Alzheimer's-associated mutations could interfere with normal nerve-to-muscle function. This suggests that at least some movement difficulties linked to the disease may arise directly in the peripheral nervous system rather than being caused entirely by degeneration in the brain.

Why Damaged Nerve Connections Can Affect Walking and Balance.

Every voluntary movement depends on successful communication between the nervous system and the muscles.

According to recent reports, at the neuromuscular junction, an electrical signal traveling along a motor neuron triggers chemical communication that causes a muscle to contract. This process makes everyday activities possible, from walking and maintaining posture to lifting objects and performing precise movements.

When the connection becomes impaired, muscles may respond less effectively to nerve signals. Depending on the severity and location of the problem, this can contribute to weakness, reduced coordination, and difficulty sustaining physical activity.

To evaluate these effects, the research team measured how consistently nerve signals produced muscle contractions and how long the muscles could continue contracting before becoming fatigued.

These measurements provided a direct assessment of how well the nerve and muscle cells worked together. They also resemble aspects of the functional testing physicians use when examining patients with movement disorders.

It has been revealed that "You can't move unless the motor circuit works," Hickman indicates. "When a doctor taps your knee to check your reflex, they're testing that exact connection.".

By demonstrating impaired nerve-to-muscle communication in a system containing no brain or spinal cord, the study provides evidence that mutations linked to familial Alzheimer's can produce effects beyond the central nervous system.

However, the experiments do not establish that these changes necessarily occur before memory loss in patients. Further research will be needed to determine how closely the laboratory findings reflect the progression of Alzheimer's in people, particularly those with the more common forms of the disease.

Could This Discovery Lead to Earlier Alzheimer's Detection?

The findings suggest a potentially important new direction for Alzheimer's research: looking beyond memory and other cognitive symptoms when investigating the disease.

If future studies confirm that changes in motor function are detectable early in certain patients, tests of walking, coordination, or nerve-to-muscle activity might eventually help identify disease-related changes before more obvious neurological symptoms develop.

The results also raise questions about treatment. Many Alzheimer's therapies are designed to address processes occurring in the brain, but medications that target the central nervous system may not necessarily correct abnormalities affecting peripheral nerves and muscles.

Understanding these separate effects could help researchers investigate treatments that protect physical function alongside cognitive health.

Human-on-a-Chip Technology Could Transform Disease Research.

Beyond the implications for Alzheimer's, the researchers see considerable potential in using human-on-a-chip systems to investigate other diseases and evaluate possible treatments.

Because these platforms contain human cells and reproduce measurable biological activities, they can help scientists observe disease-related changes in conditions that more closely resemble human physiology than some conventional experimental models.

This approach may be particularly useful in drug development, where researchers need to understand not only how a potential treatment affects individual cells but also how it influences interactions between different tissues.

Such systems can also uncover biological effects that may be difficult to detect in animal experiments, potentially helping researchers identify promising therapies and recognize limitations earlier in development.

For Hickman, the progress represents the culmination of three decades of work devoted to understanding disease through more realistic laboratory models.

"These systems let us study disease in a way that's closer to what actually happens in the human body, and that's what we need to develop better treatments," he states.

Road signs are short, sweet, and sometimes downright goofy. However, they're not always easy to understand. When a picture is worth a thousand words, deciphering signage with diagonal black-and-yellow stripes or arrows pointing in opposite directions is akin to playing Pictionary with toddlers: what is that shape supposed to mean?! Adding a few words can create even more ambiguity, like Pennsylvania's contribution to the worst road signs list. Which brings us to the narrows.

Recent findings suggest that various warning signs are used for narrowing roadways. The self-explanatory ones are emblazoned with the phrases "road narrows" and "narrow bridge." Less informative is the pictorial variation featuring an hourglass-like outline that may or may not be accompanied by vertical dashes down the middle — the figure's "hips" reference the road narrowing. Regardless of which version you see, the rules of engagement remain the same: proceed with caution.

The Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD), which is managed by the U.S. DOT's Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), sets the standards for all traffic-flow-related communications, including road markings, signs, and signals. Per the MUTCD, Road Narrows signs are part of the W5 series, which includes cautions for underpasses. Standardized to be yellow, warning signs will vary in shape. For the W5s, the MUTCD settled on a diamond.

Sources indicate that you'll also find them only in specific places. Plenty of driving lanes narrow and widen, but only when the path is shrunk to a certain width will you come across a W5 sign. The exception is low-volume local streets with speed limits of 30 mph or less. At those speeds, you're likely able to see oncoming traffic.

It has been revealed that according to the MUTCD, a road's width must diminish so abruptly and sharply that opposing traffic cannot simultaneously pass at posted speed limits. For bridges, culverts, and underpasses, warnings are issued following the surface-street rules, as well as when the two-way road's clearance is 16 to 18 feet across. This measurement includes the shoulder, if there is one.

The guidance suggests warnings be posted roughly 155 to 325 feet ahead of narrowings in 25 mph sections and up to 990 feet in 55 mph sectors. If visibility is impaired due to curves or grades, those distances can be adjusted. In construction zones, especially dangerous highway work, the W5s switch to work-zone orange and should appear prior to lane tapers, while a second reminder can be placed closer to the work area.

Industry observers note that so, what should you do when you see a narrows sign? Because it's not a road closure and the number of lanes can be unchanged, you simply continue on. Just keep your vehicle centered and take things slow and easy, especially if there's oncoming traffic. If a large vehicle approaches, like a bus or truck, consider yielding and letting it through. Room to pass will be limited, even if there is a shoulder.

On bridges, stick to your side of the road, reduce your speed, and definitely watch out for outside mirrors. If the bridge is too narrow for two vehicles, the rule of thumb is whoever arrives first gets dibs. If there's no room, there's no point in forcing your way through. Although these signs don't say how long the road narrows, the early heads-up gives you time to prepare.
